title: Tableau AI Features: Tableau Next, Pulse and Tableau Agent
summary: Tableau Next, Pulse and Tableau Agent reviewed: how Tableau's AI works, its limits, and whether nao, open source, can replace a dashboarding tool like Tableau.
body_markdown:
Tableau's AI answers questions about Tableau content, and only there.


**Tableau AI** is Salesforce's set of AI features for Tableau: **Tableau Next** (the newer platform with semantic models and conversational features), **Tableau Pulse** with **Tableau Agent in Pulse** (metric summaries you can question), and **Tableau Agent** for authoring vizzes. It suits teams whose analytics already lives in Tableau Cloud and Salesforce. What it does not give your data team is a way to test the answers, to see what users were told, or to choose the model underneath. **nao** is the open source alternative: an analytics agent your data team builds, tests and monitors on any warehouse, with live dashboards, data apps and slide decks built from a question.


This review comes from our own tests of Tableau, Tableau's documentation as reported by practitioners, and what Tableau customers told us this month.


## Tableau Next, Pulse and Tableau Agent: what each one does


Each option comes with its limit:


- **Tableau Next** : Salesforce's newer analytics platform, which "brings in AI-assisted analytics, semantic models and conversational features", though "license costs and administration need a hard look before signing" ([Analytics Insight](https://www.analyticsinsight.net/amp/story/apps/top-10-business-intelligence-platforms-for-enterprises-in-2026) ). Salesforce pitches **Tableau Agent** with it as "a trusted, always-on AI agent for data prep, exploration, and conversational analytics" ([Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/ap/news/press-releases/2026/11/24/jne-accelerates-growth-with-salesforce-modernizing-sales-operations-and-improving-conversion-rates-by-20/) ). Your context lives in Salesforce's semantic models.
- **Tableau Pulse** : every follower of a metric gets a headline value, the change against a comparison period and a ranked list of insights. It runs on **Tableau Cloud only** , and every metric is built on a published Tableau data source ([DataStudios](https://www.datastudios.org/post/how-to-explore-metrics-tableau-agent-in-pulse-check-numbers) ).
- **Tableau Agent in Pulse** : a conversational layer across a group of followed metrics. It is a **Tableau+** feature and needs a Salesforce org connected to Tableau Cloud with Einstein generative AI set up.
- **Tableau Agent for authoring** : opens in a worksheet, suggests questions, builds vizzes and helps with calculations. It helps people who build in Tableau, it does not answer any question on your warehouse ([nao vs Tableau](https://getnao.io/resources/compare/tableau/) ).
- **Tableau MCP** : open source developer tools to query published data sources and get views from Claude or other AI apps. In our test, building a dashboard through it was painful.


## How Tableau AI works


Pulse splits the work in two. According to Tableau's documentation, as summarized by DataStudios, the insights come from "standardized, deterministic statistical models", and generative AI writes the language of the summaries around those facts.


That makes the metric definition the whole game. DataStudios gives the example: a definition filter as ordinary as **excluding returned orders** can change which region Pulse names as the top driver of a monthly change. Their advice to analysts is two jobs: ask questions the service can answer, and check that the metric behind the answer is defined the way the business thinks it is.


Tableau Agent for authoring reads field names, aliases and field comments, so describing your fields improves it. It runs on the Einstein Trust Layer, which can mask PII before data reaches the LLM.


Tableau users are still testing what Tableau Next can show. One practitioner who compared a Tableau Next Data App with a Tableau Next dashboard on the Superstore sample wrote that Tableau Next had been hard to recommend for its range of expression ([X](https://x.com/marreta27_jp/status/2124449903598506066) ).


## How much does Tableau AI cost?


No amounts here: they change, check Tableau's pricing page. What the features need:


- Pulse: Tableau Cloud, turned on by a site administrator. The AI settings are separate switches, off by default.
- Tableau Agent in Pulse and Tableau Agent for authoring: **Tableau+** , plus a Salesforce org with Einstein for the Pulse agent. Sites without Tableau+ can try it with a 60-day trial.


Tableau's sales argument this renewal season is that its AI agent comes without credit billing. The real cost is elsewhere: per-user licences for every viewer, and the work of rebuilding your definitions as Tableau data sources and semantic models, work that only serves Salesforce's assistants.


## Tableau AI limitations


1. **The model is old, and it isn't yours.** A data leader renewing Tableau this month asked which model runs Tableau's agent, in a data community Slack we are part of. Tableau's answer: **GPT-4o** , a model from 2024. OpenAI now lists GPT-4o as deprecated, and Microsoft retires GPT-4o version 2024-05-13 on Azure on **January 14, 2027** , replaced by GPT-5.1 ([Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirements) ). You pay for a premium tier and get a model newer ones have overtaken, and you can't switch: the models, the trust layer and the org setup come from Salesforce.
2. **The AI helps authors, it doesn't answer the business.** Tableau Agent works inside a worksheet, for people who already build in Tableau. A sales manager with a question still files a ticket or hunts for the right dashboard and filter.
3. **Dashboards are still built by hand.** Every new question that no dashboard covers means a new viz, built and maintained by an analyst. The Tableau MCP doesn't fix that: building a dashboard through it was painful in our test.
4. **Context stops at Tableau.** The agent knows your published data sources and metric definitions. Your dbt docs, business rules and the tables nobody published in Tableau stay outside, and there is no dbt sync: definitions get rebuilt by hand.
5. **Nobody tests the answers.** Pulse is honest that the numbers depend on the definition, then leaves the checking to the analyst, one answer at a time. We found **no evaluation framework** to measure how often an answer is right before rolling it out.
6. **The data team doesn't see what users were told.** We found **no observability** on AI answers: no log of the questions asked, the query that ran and the answer given.
7. **The AI depends on your licence tier and your cloud.** Pulse is Tableau Cloud only, the conversational agents need Tableau+ and a Salesforce org with Einstein. Self-hosted Tableau Server sites are left out.


## Should you build your analytics agent on Tableau?


Not if your data team wants to own it. It is lock-in by design:


- **Your context lives in Tableau's format.** Published data sources and semantic models, readable only by Tableau's assistants or an MCP client you have to test yourself.
- **Your model is Salesforce's choice.** When a better model ships, you wait for Tableau to adopt it. When a model is retired, Tableau decides what replaces it.
- **Your AI depends on the license tier.** The conversational features sit behind Tableau+ and a Salesforce org.
- **Your agent's ceiling is Salesforce's roadmap.** If Tableau Agent doesn't read your dbt project, you wait.


## Can nao really replace a dashboarding tool like Tableau?


For what most dashboards are used for, yes. Look at what people do with Tableau: check a few KPIs, filter by country or plan, get the weekly report in their inbox, send a deck to the leadership team. nao does each of these from a question, on your warehouse, with numbers your data team has tested.


What you use Tableau for How nao does it


A dashboard per topic A **story** : KPIs, charts, tabs and filters, built by the agent from one request


Keeping dashboards up to date **Live stories** refresh on a schedule, and the narrative is rewritten to match the new numbers


Branded reports and decks for leadership **Custom stories** : interactive data apps and slide decks in your own brand


Subscriptions and alerts **Automations** : scheduled reports and conditional alerts by email or Slack


"Can you add a chart for X?" tickets Ask in chat, then add the chart to the story


Sharing Share with the project or specific people, recipients keep chatting from the story, export to PDF or HTML


Moving existing dashboards` nao migrate tableau` , checked chart by chart against the Tableau export


### Stories: dashboards built from a question


Ask "Build a dashboard of revenue by country" and the agent writes the SQL, runs it on your warehouse and builds a[story](https://getnao.io/blog/how-to-turn-chat-with-data-into-shareable-stories/) : KPIs, charts, tabs, and filters on date range, country and plan. Turn on **Live story** and it refreshes on a schedule. Every save is versioned. You edit it in a block editor, and humans can edit a chart directly instead of re-prompting.


### Custom stories: data apps and slide decks in your brand


Tableau is known for polished visuals. With **custom stories** , the agent builds interactive data apps and slide decks. Set a theme once, generated from your website, an image, a PDF or your brand kit, and every story looks like your own internal app. Here, one message ("Use our Kova brand design") turns the same revenue story into a branded, live slide deck.


### Chat for every question no dashboard answers


The questions that never get a dashboard are most of them. In nao, anyone asks in plain English and gets the SQL, the chart and the answer in one thread, in the nao web app,[Slack](https://getnao.io/blog/setup-ai-analytics-slack-bot-open-source/) ,[Microsoft Teams](https://getnao.io/blog/setup-ai-analytics-teams-bot-open-source/) , or in Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor through the[nao MCP app](https://getnao.io/blog/launching-nao-mcp-app/) , which renders the same charts and stories there.


### Automations instead of subscriptions


[Automations](https://getnao.io/blog/launching-nao-automations/) run the agent on a schedule: "Every Monday, email me the weekly business review with charts", or "Check daily if revenue dropped more than 10%, only notify me if it did". The agent reasons on the data, so it can skip the notification when there is nothing to report. Every run lands in the Feed.


### Move a Tableau dashboard to nao


nao ships a Tableau migration. Run` nao migrate tableau configure` once (Tableau server, site and a personal access token), then ask the agent to migrate a published workbook with the[migrate-tableau-workbook skill](https://github.com/getnao/nao/tree/main/skills/migrate-tableau-workbook) .


` nao migrate tableau "<workbook>"` exports the workbook's dashboards, worksheets, filters, and a CSV and image of each worksheet. The agent then rebuilds each dashboard as a tab of a nao story, with queries on your warehouse, and **compares each query with the Tableau CSV** before delivering. What it can't match exactly goes in a "Migration notes" tab instead of being guessed.


Start with the dashboards people open every week, keep Tableau running while you check them side by side, and switch viewers over once the numbers match.


## nao vs Tableau AI


**nao is open source (Apache 2.0).** Self-host it or run it on nao Cloud, bring your own LLM, read every line of the agent.


Tableau AI (Next, Pulse, Agent) nao


License Proprietary, per-user licences, AI on Tableau+ **Open source, Apache 2.0**


LLM Salesforce's choice (GPT-4o, per Tableau this month) Yours: Claude, GPT, Gemini, Mistral, Bedrock, Ollama, switch any time


Context Published Tableau data sources, semantic models Files in your repo: schemas, dbt docs,` RULES.md` , semantic layer, skills


Who it serves Tableau authors Anyone with a question, and the data team that governs it


Dashboards Built by hand Stories and custom stories built from a question, live refresh


Interfaces Tableau Cloud, Pulse digests nao web app, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor through the MCP app


Scheduled reports Subscriptions Automations with conditions, by email or Slack


Evaluation None found in our test` nao test` on your own questions


Observability None found on AI answers Every question logged with its SQL, thumbs up / down, Chats Replay, context recommendations


Hosting Tableau Cloud for the AI features nao Cloud or self-hosted with Docker


## Test it like code


A dashboard was trusted because an analyst built it. An agent is trusted because the data team tested it:


1. ` pip install nao-core` ,` nao init` , connect your warehouse ([database docs](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-builder/databases) ) and` nao sync` . Or sign up on[nao Cloud](https://getnao.io/blog/launching-nao-agentic-bi-builder/) and do it from the UI.
2. Add your[dbt repo](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-builder/repos) and your business rules in` RULES.md` , following our[context engineering guide](https://getnao.io/blog/how-to-do-context-engineering-for-data-teams/) .
3. Write 20 to 40 real questions with their reference SQL and run[nao test](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-engineering/evaluation) . The "excluding returned orders" kind of definition becomes a test, not a hope.
4. Roll it out and watch real usage: when a user flags a wrong answer, click **Save as test** on it, fix the context, rerun the suite.[Context recommendations](https://getnao.io/blog/launching-nao-context-recommendations/) point at the gaps you didn't think to test.


This loop took our own agent[from 45% to 86% right answers](https://getnao.io/blog/improve-analytics-agent-reliability-steps/) . See how other tools did in our[20-tool benchmark](https://getnao.io/blog/ai-data-agents-compared/) , how the same lock-in plays out in our[Power BI AI review](https://getnao.io/blog/power-bi-ai-review/) and[Snowflake Cortex review](https://getnao.io/blog/snowflake-cortex-review/) , and the full method in the[agentic analytics playbook](https://getnao.io/resources/playbook/) .
